title: The Matsya Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa. It presents itself as the teaching given by Vishnu in his fish incarnation to Manu, the survivor of the flood, and was compiled over several centuries.
description: The Matsya Purana begins with the flood and the fish that tows Manu's boat, and continues into a survey of the old learning: creation and the ages, the genealogies, the duties of kings, the laws of inheritance, the making and ornament of images and temples, and the meritorious gifts, vows and pilgrimage of an ordinary religious life.
historicalContext: Among the older Puranas, the Matsya is a principal source for the history of Indian art and architecture: its chapters on the measurements of the temple and on the proportion of images are quoted by later builders' manuals and by modern historians of art.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit text of chapters 1 to 176 as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
